input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the new enabled flag is stored on the retry object but only checked inside wraps(), so the direct call, iterator and async paths retry regardless of it
- failure path: Retrying(enabled=False, stop=stop_after_attempt(3))(f) where f raises ValueError: f is called three times and RetryError is raised, identical to enabled=True; only the decorator path honors the flag

Reviewer finding
- description: The enabled flag is checked only by decorated wrappers, so calling Retrying(enabled=False) directly still retries. AsyncRetrying has the same gap.
- rationale: For example, Retrying(enabled=False, stop=stop_after_attempt(3))(f), where f raises ValueError, enters the unchanged retry loop and calls f three times before raising RetryError. Users of the direct-call API therefore still experience repeated calls and retry delays despite explicitly disabling retries.
critique: The finding matches the label's mechanism: the enabled flag is checked only in the decorator wrapper, so direct calls (and async) still retry. It also gives the same failure example of three calls followed by RetryError.
